fresh_topic_ideas: A 62‑year‑old man presented with recurrent abdominal pain; CT showed a calcified pancreatic mass later identified as primary pancreatic sarcoidosis, a never‑reported entity.

A 45‑year‑old patient presented with unexplained hyponatremia; serum osmolality was low, and a brain MRI displayed a posterior pituitary lesion later diagnosed as Langerhans cell histiocytosis, first adult case reported.

A 28‑year‑old female presented with acute bilateral lower‑extremity weakness; EMG showed demyelinating neuropathy, and serum anti‑MOG antibodies indicated a newly described variant of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

A 57‑year‑old man arrived with episodic chest pain; coronary angiography was normal, yet cardiac MRI displayed diffuse infiltration later identified as cardiac involvement of Erdheim‑Chester disease, first cardiac case reported.

A 22‑year‑old student experienced severe headaches; CSF analysis revealed elevated protein, and next‑generation sequencing discovered a novel ALK‑fusion tumor causing leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, the first such case.

A 73‑year‑old woman presented with sudden visual field loss; fundus exam showed optic disc edema, and OCT identified peripapillary retinal angiomatous proliferation, later classified as an atypical ocular manifestation of Behçet disease.

A 5‑year‑old child presented with unexplained seizures; EEG revealed focal spikes, and metabolic panel showed markedly low pyridoxal‑5′‑phosphate, leading to the discovery of a novel PLP‑dependent enzyme deficiency.

A 68‑year-old female reported persistent pruritus; skin biopsy showed atypical lymphoid infiltrates, and molecular testing identified a previously undescribed cutaneous manifestation of adult‑onset Still’s disease.

A 34‑year‑old man arrived with recurrent epistaxis; nasal endoscopy revealed a vascular lesion, and histopathology diagnosed a rare sinonasal hemangiopericytoma, the first case linked to a STAT3 mutation.

A 49‑year-old woman experienced unexplained hypertension; renal ultrasound was normal, yet renal artery Doppler showed stenosis caused by fibromuscular dysplasia associated with a novel NOTCH2 variant.

A 27‑year‑old female presented with intermittent dysphagia; barium swallow highlighted a esophageal stricture, and biopsy identified a unique lymphocytic esophagitis associated with a new HLA‑DQ allele.

A 60‑year-old man had progressive gait instability; spinal MRI displayed diffuse white‑matter lesions, and CSF analysis detected anti‑GFAP antibodies, marking the first reported case of GFAP‑autoimmune astrocytopathy in adults.

A 15‑year-old adolescent presented with rapid weight loss; endocrine labs showed low cortisol, and adrenal imaging revealed bilateral adrenal hyperplasia due to a rare ACTH‑producing pheochromocytoma, never before described.
